records.verificationNote: Read PDL pp.40-42 directly (pypdf). The 'Clinical PA required' line printed under the class heading on p.41 is treated as applying to preferred agents too. Most products here (Ritalin, Concerta, Focalin, Methylin, Jornay, Cotempla, Aptensio, Relexxii, Quillivant) appear on the Common Formulary as carve-outs (#, billed fee-for-service, CF p.119-123), so the FFS program applies the Single PDL. Azstarys, Daytrana and brand Metadate do not appear on the CF (Quillichew ER does, as a carve-out on CF p.253). Preferred pick is generic IR, so no brand-over-generic BOGL. Quantity limits apply (QL document not retrieved). [Sonnet check 2026-10-21: Corrected Quillichew: it IS on the CF (p.253, #). Verified preferred/non-preferred lists on PDL pp.41-42. PDL p.6 header: "Preferred agents do not require prior authorization, except as noted"; the PDL has no legend defining non-preferred, but the Common Formulary tags them "PDL-NP PA" (e.g. CF p.73 Zetia, p.7 ACE inhibitors) and preferred as "*PDL-P". Class PA applied to preferred agents on class-note wording only; CF has no PA flag for carve-outs, so inferred, not confirmed.]

records.verificationNote: Read from the PDL text layer, pp.22-23 (section 'Central Nervous System Agents - Drugs for Attention Deficit Disorder'). Legend p.5: E = may be excluded from coverage or subject to PA in CT, NJ and NY; ST = step therapy; QL = quantity limit. E-flagged brands are recorded as outcome 'pa' because the legend names PA as the NY mechanism; the document does not separate exclusion from PA. Concerta brand is E-flagged while generic methylphenidate ER (osm) is covered tier 2 QL, so the plan does not prefer the brand (boglActive false). Daytrana and Adhansia do not appear in this PDL text. Methylin (tier 4) is not separately assessed. Sig is standard FDA labeling, not the PDL. [Reused 2026-10-21 for uhc-md: same national UHC commercial PDL document as ny-uhc-commercial; Sonnet-checked in the NY pass. NY-specific "E" (may be excluded in NY) flags apply to NY plans; outside CT/NJ/NY the PDL legend (p.5) says E-flagged drugs may be excluded from coverage, so they are recorded as non-formulary here.] [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21)]
